alyssa: FYI morning spike in single-queue saturation in us-east-1 around 03:04 UTC. p95 token latency jumped from ~120ms -> 1.6s for ~90s, then dropped. Not a full outage but dropped a handful of requests to 503s.
ops-bot: ALERT: queue_backlog > 1000 for 65s on fleet-gpu-prod-us-east-1 (severity: warning)
mike: logs/metrics? any correlated autoscale events or spot reclaim?
alyssa: attaching quick numbers: queue_len peaked 1184, warm_pool_idle 0 -> 0, spinup_inflight 12, new_nodes_provisioned 0 during the spike. No spot reclaim in cloud events.
zara: this looks like a coordination/thundering-herd on admission when many cold sessions hit the same placement group. warm-pool size being 0 means cold-start pressure.
sam: cost team will yell if we overprovision. can we mitigate without big buffer increases?
zara: yes — proposal: switch from continuous prewarm to jittered "pulse" pre-provisions + soft admission fuse. idea: instead of keeping N idle, schedule small randomized pulses across zones to spread spinups and add a token-based soft-fuse to shed or queue beyond headroom.
mike: can you sketch config? want something we can canary quickly.
zara: sketch: ```
# pseudo-config
warm_pulse:
  enabled: true
  target_per_zone: 6
  pulse_interval_s: 60
  jitter_pct: 0.3   # randomize +-30% around interval
admission:
  mode: soft_fuse
  token_bucket_capacity: 200
  token_refill_per_s: 10
  soft_drop_threshold: 0.85  # when usage >85% slow-queue instead of hard-drop
  cooldown_s: 45
```
alyssa: nice. also add a short holdback window after a successful pulse to avoid immediately triggering another pulse (debounce). pulse -> holdback -> pulse with jitter.
mike: admission soft_fuse + token bucket makes sense. we should also add very small randomized start_delay on new node spinup (1-8s) to avoid multiple nodes hitting registry at same instant.
sam: cost check: if we do target_per_zone:6 in 4 zones that's 24 pre-provisioned GPUs max during a pulse, but since it's pulse-based they will age out if unused. estimate monthly delta < 6% for typical load — acceptable if it stabilizes latency.
alyssa: suggestion: canary plan: rollout to us-west-2 first, 1% of traffic, 2-hour observation window, key metrics: p95 token latency, queue_len, spinup_inflight, failed_admission_rate, cost burn rate.
zara: add a regression alert: if failed_admission_rate increases >2x or p95 latency worsens >15% revert automatically.
mike: implementation steps I can do today: 1) add admission toggles behind feature-flag 2) implement pulse scheduler with jitter 3) add telemetry points (pulse_count, pulse_success, pulse_retries) 4) canary rollout script -> `./scripts/canary-rollout --zone us-west-2 --pct 1`
alyssa: I can take ownership of the runbook and the rollback playbook. sam can confirm cost guardrails. ops-bot: CREATED ticket INFRA-3412 for canary and rollout runbook.
ops-bot: ticket INFRA-3412 assigned to mike, priority: high, due: 2026-03-19
sam: I'll sign off on cost if the canary dashboard shows <3% burn and latency improves.
mike: plan to push behind ff and roll canary in 2 hours if no objections.
alyssa: go for it. please post snapshot dashboards here when canary starts. :thumbsup:
zara: also recommend a follow-up to examine admission metrics per placement-group; if some PGs consistently attract bursts we should shard differently.
alyssa: agreed. follow-up ticket after canary if stable.
mike: starting PR now. small command snippet for observers: `kubectl apply -f autoscale/pulse-config.yaml --context=us-west-2`
alyssa: thanks all. keeping channel updated. :white_check_mark:
